_directive: losslessly compressed, token-efficient, information-dense, fully detailed, machine-facing; optimized for model parsing over human readability

analysis.fixed_dense_envelope: dense mode caps nodes at 19-24 and edges at 32-40 REGARDLESS of how many domains are batched into one KB.
analysis.batching_effect: 2 domains in one KB -> ~8 nodes/domain vs ~19-21 nodes when solo. IR coverage fell 19->8 nodes = ~58% per-domain depth LOSS.
analysis.token_effect: combined output (24711 tok) ~= ONE KB's worth, NOT two; batching does not raise total output, it SPLITS the fixed budget.
analysis.quality_gate: all three passed structurally/formula-wise; degradation is in COVERAGE/DEPTH per domain, not in validity.
analysis.output_ceiling: single dense KB ranged 24.7k-37.1k est tokens, none truncated; ~37k (run1) sits in the upper band of a single-response output. Treat one dense KB as one full heavy session output.
analysis.concurrency: 3 helpers ran in parallel successfully (~10-15 min each); fan-out is the scaling lever.

decision.rule: ONE coherent domain per dense KB run to preserve full per-domain depth. Do NOT batch multiple domains into a single dense KB.
decision.scaling_strategy: parallel_fanout_one_domain_per_dense_kb (run many single-domain helpers concurrently, gate each, commit each)

mode_policy.dense: high-value / broad domains needing full depth
mode_policy.compact: low-value or very narrow domains (user: low-value things may use other modes)

decision.narrow_domain_exception: if a 'domain' is genuinely narrow (would be over-covered by 19-24 dense nodes), prefer standard/compact for it rather than co-batching two narrow domains into one dense KB.
decision.run4_skipped_reason: RUN_4 was user-conditional ('only if quality does not degrade'). Degradation IS demonstrated at 2 domains; the fixed dense node budget guarantees 4 domains -> ~5 nodes/domain (worse). Empirical RUN_4 would only confirm further loss.

implications_for_pipeline.phase_A4_mass_generation: batch the knowledge_searcher taxonomy as 1 domain per dense KB; fan out helpers in parallel; gate + commit each.
implications_for_pipeline.phase_B: same unit (1 domain/KB); optional DOMAIN_ADAPTER_SCHEMA_GENERATION per idea to constrain each KB.
implications_for_pipeline.estimated_cost_per_domain: ~25k-37k est output tokens + ~100k-115k helper working tokens per dense KB (from this sweep).
